# Overview

This dataset contains carbon and oxygen isotope measurements and
calculated CO2 yields from one instrument run of rhodochrosite
(MnCO3) samples reacted with phosphoric acid at 72 °C. The samples
were prepared in two grain-size fractions: less than 74 µm and
149–250 µm. They were analyzed after different reaction durations.

The workbook also includes measurements of carbonate reference
materials used for isotope normalization and assessment of
analytical performance.

# Data description

The Excel workbook contains measurements from one instrument run
of rhodochrosite samples reacted with phosphoric acid at 72 °C.
It also contains reference-material measurements and calculations
used to normalize isotope values and estimate CO2 yield.

The main information in the workbook includes:

- Sample identifiers and grain-size labels.
- Acid injection dates and reaction durations.
- Instrument measurements and sample preparation values.
- Carbon isotope values (δ13C).
- Oxygen isotope values of the released CO2 (δ18O CO2).
- Peak-area information and calculated CO2 yields.
- Measurements of reference materials, including NBS 18,
  NBS 19, and Carrara.

# Experimental design, materials and methods

Rhodochrosite (MnCO3) samples were prepared in two grain-size
fractions: less than 74 µm and 149–250 µm. Samples were reacted
with phosphoric acid at 72 °C for different reaction durations.

The carbon dioxide (CO2) released during digestion was analyzed
for carbon and oxygen isotope composition. Carbonate reference
materials, including NBS 18 and NBS 19, were measured during the
instrument run and used for isotope normalization. Carrara was
also included as a reference material.

# Value of the data

- The dataset provides measurements of CO2 yield and carbon and
  oxygen isotope values for rhodochrosite reacted at 72 °C.

- The two grain-size fractions allow users to compare digestion
  behaviour for fine and coarse samples.

- The different reaction durations allow users to examine how CO2
  yield and measured isotope values change over time.

- The reference-material measurements provide information for
  assessing the analytical performance of the instrument run.
